# Automatic texture atlas

@difference Extension: small clamped textures that are loaded from files are merged into shared images by the runtime, so that scenes with many of them need fewer draw calls; [TextureAtlas](TextureAtlas) turns it off.

The 3D renderer draws everything that has the same mesh, texture and state in one call, and each different texture breaks that. When a program loads many small textures (sprites, icons, particles), BlitzLLVM copies them into pages of 1024 by 1024 pixels at the next [RenderWorld](RenderWorld) and gives every texture a view of its rectangle, the same as [AtlasTexture](AtlasTexture) makes. Each rectangle has a border of one pixel that repeats the edge of the picture, so what the texture clamped to is what it still reads. The result is pixel for pixel the same as without the merging.

Only textures that this cannot change are merged: loaded from a file, at most 256 by 256 pixels, 8 bits per channel, clamped (a repeating texture would read its neighbours), without mip maps, and not a sphere or cube map, render target, sheet of frames, atlas or sRGB texture. A texture that has a sampler of its own is left alone. Coordinates outside 0 to 1 on a clamped texture, which a mesh can have, read the neighbouring picture instead of the edge; set [TextureAtlas](TextureAtlas) to False, or give the texture flag 8 or leave out the clamp flags, if a program depends on that.

[TextureBuffer](TextureBuffer), [ScaleTexture](ScaleTexture), [PositionTexture](PositionTexture), [RotateTexture](RotateTexture) and [SetTextureSampler](SetTextureSampler) need a picture of their own, so a merged texture gets one back when they are used on it, and is not merged again. The rectangles of freed textures are not reused; a page is freed with its last texture. Merging costs a copy on the graphics card for every texture, which adds a little to loading.
